punchline: Among Tokyo teenagers, Rheingold found, a text message counted as being there, and arriving late was fine if you stayed in touch by text.
thirty_sec: Howard Rheingold walked Tokyo's streets with flocks of teenagers who converged on public places, steered by text messages. An anthropologist he cites says the phone freed them from the family land line, and over 90 percent of Tokyo teens had one. Texting someone counted as being present, and being late was fine if you texted. Rheingold calls groups like this smart mobs: people who act in concert without knowing each other.
